chunks: Ali (ibn Ibrahim) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who set out on a journey, then it became apparent to him that he should stay (reside), while he was in his prayer. He said: 'He completes (his prayer) if it becomes apparent to him that he should stay.'
ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do with his prayer if he decides to stay in a place while he is already praying?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise moment of transition in prayer status: the intent to settle (iqamah) must be present during the prayer to invalidate the traveler's privilege of shortening (qasr). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the state of travel is determined by the actual condition at the time of prayer, not merely the initial departure, ensuring the worshipper fulfills the full four-rak'ah obligation once residency is established.
